## option_sets

A set of functional option collections to export

#### Type: `array`

## option_set

A generated options object and its functional option helpers.
AsList and AsIterator convert an object into functional options while
preserving its enabled state and Clone semantics.
Interface arguments naming this generated object use a list of functional
options by default, or an iterator when iterator is true. A final list
argument is variadic. CLI configuration retains an editable options object,
even when list or iterator is specified; convert it at the SDK call boundary.

#### Type: `object`

| Property | Type | Required | Possible values | Conditional | Default | Description |
| -------- | ---- | -------- | --------------- | ----------- | ------- | ----------- |
| name | `string` | ✅ | string |  |  | The name of the functional option collection |
| description | `string` | ✅ | string |  |  | A human-readable description.<br />Multiline YAML descriptions using `\|` are supported. |
| functions | `array` | ✅ | [option_function](#option_function) |  |  |  |
| package | `string` |  | [`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`](https://regex101.com/?regex=%5E%5BA-Za-z_%5D%5BA-Za-z0-9_%5D%2A%24) |  | `"options"` | The package the functional option collection is defined in.<br />Defaults to `options`. |
| deprecation_notice | `object` |  | [deprecation_notice](#deprecation_notice) |  |  |  |
| enable_mode | `string` |  | `independent` `together` |  | `"independent"` | Choose whether option parameters are enabled independently or together.<br /><br />independent (the default): each parameter has a separate wrapper containing<br />its value and its own Enabled flag. A generated helper enables only the<br />parameters it sets.<br /><br />together: the generated struct contains one Enabled bool for the entire<br />option set and the parameter fields directly, for example ExcludeFiles<br />[]string. Calling any generated With... or Without... helper sets the<br />shared Enabled flag to true.<br /><br />In together mode:<br />- Field-level validation, such as enum and pattern checks, runs only when<br />  Enabled is true.<br />- Rules involving other fields, such as forbidden_when, always run.<br />  Use parameter: Enabled to allow or forbid values depending on whether<br />  the option set is enabled.<br />- Fields use the parameter names declared in the manifest. value_field<br />  overrides are not supported because there are no parameter wrappers. |
| enable_mode | `const` |  | `together` | **If** infer_enabled_from_non_empty_values = True |  |  |
| infer_enabled_from_non_empty_values | `boolean` |  | boolean |  | `false` | This is only valid when `enable_mode: together` is selected.<br /><br />When `enable_mode: together` is selected, infer `Enabled = true` during<br />validation and `AsList`/`AsIterator` snapshot conversion whenever any<br />generated option field contains a non-empty value.<br /><br />This is useful for selector-style together-mode option sets such as<br />overwrite include/exclude lists.<br /><br />Do not enable this when non-empty default values should remain disabled:<br />if a default value is non-empty, it also counts towards inference. |

| mapstructure_tag | `string` |  | string | The mapstructure tag of the value field; defaults to the snake_case value field name. |

## parameter_value_constraint

A value-based constraint against another parameter.
This definition is used by parameter `constraints` for relationships that
depend on another parameter's presence or value.

#### Type: `object`

| Property | Type | Required | Possible values | Default | Description |
| -------- | ---- | -------- | --------------- | ------- | ----------- |
| parameter | `string` | ✅ | string |  | The name of the parameter being evaluated |
| operator | `string` |  | `present` `absent` `equals` `not_equals` `in` `not_in` | `"present"` | The comparison performed against the parameter |
| value | `None` |  | None |  | The value used by operators such as equals or not_equals |
| values | `array` |  | Any type |  | Values used by operators such as in or not_in |

## parameter_value_comparison_constraint

A value comparison against another parameter.
This definition is used by parameter `constraints.parameter_value` when
the current parameter value must equal or differ from another parameter
value.
Unlike `required_when` or `forbidden_when`, this is not a rule about
whether the parameter itself is present. It is a rule about which values
of the current parameter are valid when compared with another parameter
value.

#### Type: `object`

| Property | Type | Required | Possible values | Default | Description |
| -------- | ---- | -------- | --------------- | ------- | ----------- |
| parameter | `string` | ✅ | string |  | The name of the parameter whose value is compared with the current parameter value |
| operator | `string` | ✅ | `present` `absent` `equals` `not_equals` `in` `not_in` |  | The comparison performed between the current parameter value and the referenced parameter value |
| when | `string` |  | `always` `empty` `not_empty` | `"always"` | Controls when this comparison is evaluated against the current parameter<br />value. `always` applies the comparison unconditionally. `empty` applies it<br />only when the current parameter value is empty according to the generator's<br />normal validation semantics. `not_empty` applies it only when the current<br />parameter value is non-empty. |

## parameter_forbidden_values_constraint

A conditional forbidden-values rule for the current parameter value.
This definition is used by parameter `constraints.forbidden_values_when`
when specific values of the current parameter become invalid depending on
another parameter value.
Unlike `required_when` or `forbidden_when`, this is not a rule about
whether the parameter itself is present. It is a rule about which values
of the current parameter are valid.

#### Type: `object`

| Property | Type | Required | Possible values | Default | Description |
| -------- | ---- | -------- | --------------- | ------- | ----------- |
| parameter | `string` | ✅ | string |  | The name of the parameter being evaluated |
| forbidden_values | `array` | ✅ | Any type |  | Values of the current parameter that are forbidden when the condition matches |
| operator | `string` |  | `present` `absent` `equals` `not_equals` `in` `not_in` | `"present"` | The comparison performed against the parameter |
| value | `None` |  | None |  | The value used by operators such as equals or not_equals |
| values | `array` |  | Any type |  | Values used by operators such as in or not_in |

## parameter_required_values_constraint

A conditional required-values rule for the current parameter value.
This definition is used by parameter `constraints.required_values_when`
when the current parameter value must be one of the specified values
depending on another parameter value.
Unlike `required_when` or `forbidden_when`, this is not a rule about
whether the parameter itself is present. It is a rule about which values
of the current parameter are valid.

#### Type: `object`

| Property | Type | Required | Possible values | Default | Description |
| -------- | ---- | -------- | --------------- | ------- | ----------- |
| parameter | `string` | ✅ | string |  | The name of the parameter being evaluated |
| required_values | `array` | ✅ | Any type |  | Values of the current parameter that are required when the condition matches |
| operator | `string` |  | `present` `absent` `equals` `not_equals` `in` `not_in` | `"present"` | The comparison performed against the parameter |
| value | `None` |  | None |  | The value used by operators such as equals or not_equals |
| values | `array` |  | Any type |  | Values used by operators such as in or not_in |

## parameter_constraints

Validation constraints applying to a parameter.
These constraints complement the existing `condition` field rather than
replacing it. Use `condition` for the current expression-style required
logic, and `constraints` for explicit cross-parameter relationships.

#### Type: `object`

| Property | Type | Required | Possible values | Default | Description |
| -------- | ---- | -------- | --------------- | ------- | ----------- |
| enum | `array` |  | string |  | Validation-oriented equivalent of the top-level `enum` field.<br />When the top-level `enum` is omitted, this can also drive generated<br />enum-backed parameter types.<br />This follows the JSON Schema `enum` keyword.<br />Reference: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/enum |
| pattern | `string` |  | string |  | Validation-oriented equivalent of the top-level `pattern` field.<br />This is only valid for scalar string-compatible values.<br />This follows the JSON Schema `pattern` keyword.<br />Reference: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/string#regular-expressions |
| required | `boolean` |  | boolean | `false` | Validation-oriented equivalent of the top-level `required` field.<br />This marks the parameter as required in the generated configuration<br />validation and documentation.<br />This is analogous to listing the containing property under JSON Schema<br />`required`.<br />Reference: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/object#required |
| nullable | `boolean` |  | boolean | `false` | Allow the value to be omitted or null while still validating the<br />nested constraints whenever a value is provided. |
| not_empty | `boolean` |  | boolean | `false` | Require the value to be non-empty according to the generator's normal<br />validation semantics. |
| contains | `string` |  | string |  | Require a scalar string-compatible value to contain the given<br />substring. |
| not_contains | `string` |  | string |  | Require a scalar string-compatible value not to contain the given<br />substring. |
| prefix | `string` |  | string |  | Require a scalar string-compatible value to start with the given<br />prefix. |
| suffix | `string` |  | string |  | Require a scalar string-compatible value to end with the given<br />suffix. |
| min_length | `integer` |  | integer |  | Minimum number of Unicode code points allowed for a scalar<br />string-compatible value.<br />This follows the JSON Schema `minLength` keyword.<br />Reference: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/string#length |
| max_length | `integer` |  | integer |  | Maximum number of Unicode code points allowed for a scalar<br />string-compatible value.<br />This follows the JSON Schema `maxLength` keyword.<br />Reference: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/string#length |
| minimum | `number` |  | number |  | Inclusive lower bound for a scalar numeric value.<br />This follows the JSON Schema `minimum` keyword.<br />Reference: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/numeric#range |
| maximum | `number` |  | number |  | Inclusive upper bound for a scalar numeric value.<br />This follows the JSON Schema `maximum` keyword.<br />Reference: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/numeric#range |
| exclusive_minimum | `number` |  | number |  | Exclusive lower bound for a scalar numeric value.<br />This follows the JSON Schema `exclusiveMinimum` keyword.<br />Reference: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/numeric#range |
| exclusive_maximum | `number` |  | number |  | Exclusive upper bound for a scalar numeric value.<br />This follows the JSON Schema `exclusiveMaximum` keyword.<br />Reference: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/numeric#range |
| multiple_of | `number` |  | number |  | Require a scalar numeric value to be an exact multiple of the given<br />positive number.<br />This follows the JSON Schema `multipleOf` keyword.<br />Reference: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/numeric#multiples |
| min_items | `integer` |  | integer |  | Minimum number of items allowed in a list or iterator value.<br />This follows the JSON Schema `minItems` keyword.<br />Reference: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/array#length |
| max_items | `integer` |  | integer |  | Maximum number of items allowed in a list or iterator value.<br />This follows the JSON Schema `maxItems` keyword.<br />Reference: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/array#length |
| unique_items | `boolean` |  | boolean | `false` | Require all items in a list or iterator value to be unique.<br />This follows the JSON Schema `uniqueItems` keyword.<br />Reference: https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/array#uniqueness |
| extension | `array` |  | string |  | Allowed filename extensions for a scalar string-compatible path value,<br />for example `.json` or `.yaml`. |
| at_least_one | `boolean` |  | boolean | `false` | Require a list or iterator value to contain at least one item.<br />This is a convenience alias for `min_items: 1`. |
| exactly_one | `boolean` |  | boolean | `false` | Require a list or iterator value to contain exactly one item.<br />This is a convenience alias for `min_items: 1` together with<br />`max_items: 1`. |
| dependent_required | `array` |  | string |  | Parameters that must be provided when this parameter is provided. |
| require_together_as_cli_flags | `boolean` |  | boolean | `false` | Whether `dependent_required` should also require the related values<br />to be passed together as CLI arguments when all referenced parameters<br />also opt in.<br />This only affects CLI argument behaviour and does not change the<br />runtime validation rules. |
| conflicts_with | `array` |  | string |  | Parameters that must not be provided when this parameter is provided. |
| parameter_value | `object` |  | [parameter_value_comparison_constraint](#parameter_value_comparison_constraint) |  |  |

## distribute_oci

Configuration for publishing multi-architecture OCI images for the generated CLI.
OCI images are useful for CI integration, reproducible builds, and users who prefer not to install the tool locally.
OCI image publication currently targets GitHub Container Registry for GitHub-hosted repositories.

#### Type: `object`

> ⚠️ Additional properties are not allowed.

| Property | Type | Required | Possible values | Description |
| -------- | ---- | -------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| description | `string` | ✅ | string | Text description applied to the OCI image metadata and registry page. |
| labels | `object` |  | [oci_map_string_string](#oci_map_string_string) | Additional OCI image labels applied to each built image.<br />These complement the default labels generated from the tool documentation<br />and repository metadata. |
| attributes | `object` |  | [oci_map_string_string](#oci_map_string_string) | Additional OCI manifest attributes applied as OCI annotations to the<br />published image manifests.<br />These complement the default OCI annotations generated from the tool<br />documentation and repository metadata. |
